B0 majority class.notes: Floor. Predicts the most frequent training label (neutral) for every input.

B1 word TF-IDF + LogReg.notes: Reference linear model on word unigrams+bigrams.

B2 word TF-IDF + LinearSVC.notes: Margin-based linear baseline, the classic strong reference for short text.

B3 char TF-IDF + LogReg.notes: Character n-grams tolerate Hausa spelling variation and dropped diacritics.

B4 word+char TF-IDF + LinearSVC.notes: Union of lexical and sub-lexical features; expected strongest classical model.

B5 counts + ComplementNB.notes: Generative reference; cheap and competitive on small messy text.

B4b word+char TF-IDF + LogReg.notes: Same features as B4 with a probabilistic linear model.

B4c word+char TF-IDF + LogReg balanced.notes: Checks whether re-weighting helps despite the balanced label distribution.

A1 with @user placeholder.notes: Tests whether the anonymisation placeholder `@user` leaks sentiment information.

A2 emoji removed.features: word_char n-grams (58,856 dims), text=text_bow minus emoji
A2 emoji removed.notes: Measures the contribution of emoji, present in 99.9% of the training tweets.

A3 emoji + @user removed.features: word_char n-grams (60,089 dims), text=text_clean minus emoji
A3 emoji + @user removed.notes: Fully de-noised view: tests whether emoji and the placeholder together explain the classical baseline's performance.
